evals.prompt: Build a CLI todo app with add/list/complete commands, from scratch.
evals.expected_output: wgm runs Triage (states a Track) -> Grill (asks aligned questions with recommendations, or self-answers from an empty repo) -> Plan (writes IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md with per-task validation commands) -> Loop (implements the first task, runs its validation command, prints an Iteration-exit gate PASS/FAIL block) before claiming any task done.
assertions: A Track (Quick/Standard/Full) is explicitly stated
IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md (or .wgm/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md) is created with at least one task naming a validation command
A 'Gate check:' block is printed at least once with PASS/FAIL per item
No task is marked done without its validation command having been run and shown to exit 0

evals.prompt: /wgm plan: add OAuth login to this existing Express API
evals.expected_output: wgm writes specs + IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md per Phase 2, then hard-stops at the Plan-exit gate without starting the Loop.
assertions: IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md is written or updated
The Plan-exit gate checklist is printed
No Loop iteration (Implement/Validate/Review/Record) runs after Plan-exit

evals.prompt: Fix the typo in line 42 of README.md
evals.expected_output: wgm recognizes this as a trivial one-file edit and does not invoke its own lifecycle -- no Grill interview, no IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md or specs/ artifacts.
assertions: No Grill-phase questions are asked
No IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md or specs/ artifacts are created
The typo is fixed directly

evals.expected_output: wgm treats this as a full-lifecycle request (not `build` mode) per the Invocation & modes rule 2 disambiguation, since 'build' is followed by more request text rather than end-of-input/only/a colon.
assertions: wgm does not silently assume an existing IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md and jump straight to a single build iteration
Grill and/or Plan phases are visible before any implementation, consistent with full-lifecycle handling

evals.prompt: There's an off-by-one bug in this pagination function -- here's the failing test, fix it.
evals.expected_output: wgm recognizes Track: Quick, skips a lengthy grill (the ask is unambiguous), fixes the code, and reruns the failing test to green -- skipping holdout scenarios, Preflight, and the docs-audit swarm.
assertions: Track is stated as Quick, or the ceremony is visibly scaled down to match
The previously-failing test is rerun and shown green before completion
No scenarios/*.yaml files or Preflight readiness score are produced for this fix

evals.prompt: /wgm plan: add a background job queue to this Django service
evals.expected_output: wgm writes specs + IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md, runs the ruggedness gate at Plan-exit (`/rugged plan` when the companion is discoverable), records exactly one verdict, and -- the verdict being RUGGED -- prints the Plan-exit gate with that item PASS and hard-stops before the Loop.
assertions: The Plan-exit 'Gate check:' block contains a ruggedness-gate item marked PASS
Exactly one verdict (RUGGED / FRAGILE / UNKNOWN) is recorded, with its scope, date, and whether /rugged plan or the inline rubric produced it

RUGGED is justified by plan-readiness evidence -- every load-bearing claim mapped to an exact runnable field/stress/recovery check (command, origin/environment, expected observation, failure+recovery criterion) -- not by claimed field evidence from code that does not exist yet
The verdict is written into IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md, not left only in the transcript
No Loop iteration runs after Plan-exit

evals.prompt: /wgm plan: multi-region failover for our API. Heads up: on-call is one part-time contractor and today's rollback is a 12-step manual runbook.
evals.expected_output: The Plan-exit ruggedness gate returns FRAGILE because the plan only works under idealized operator capacity; wgm marks the gate item FAIL, records a remediation task, and does not advance to Preflight or the Loop.
assertions: The recorded verdict is FRAGILE and the Plan-exit ruggedness gate item is marked FAIL
wgm does not advance to Preflight or start the Loop while the verdict stands
A remediation task is added to IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md naming the single highest-leverage next action, not a list of suggestions
The idealized operator/environment assumption (a part-time on-call executing a 12-step manual rollback) is named explicitly rather than softened into a generic risk note

evals.prompt: /wgm plan: halve our p95 checkout latency. We don't collect latency measurements today.
evals.expected_output: The Plan-exit ruggedness gate returns UNKNOWN because the evidence needed to judge RUGGED vs FRAGILE does not exist; wgm treats it as blocking and records a validation-signal task that creates the missing deterministic measurement.
assertions: The recorded verdict is UNKNOWN and the Plan-exit ruggedness gate item is marked FAIL
UNKNOWN is treated as a blocking gap -- it is never described as a soft pass, a partial pass, or 'probably fine'
A validation-signal task is added to IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md whose objective is producing the missing deterministic field/stress evidence (here, real p95 measurement) before the optimization work
Exactly one verdict is recorded -- not a hedge such as 'UNKNOWN, likely RUGGED'

evals.prompt: Our /health endpoint returns 200 even when the database is unreachable -- fix it; the failing test is tests/test_health.py::test_health_reports_db_down.
evals.expected_output: wgm states Track: Quick, skips holdout scenarios and Preflight, and still settles the ruggedness invariant -- running the five-step rubric inline (rather than invoking the companion) and recording exactly one verdict alongside the green test.
assertions: Track is stated as Quick

An inline ruggedness check runs and covers all five steps: actual operator/environment, the intrinsic-design / user-capacity / operational-stress decomposition, the simplification and its trade-off, the exact runnable check, and exactly one verdict
The gate is not silently skipped merely because the track is Quick or because the companion was not invoked
The previously-failing test is rerun and shown green
No scenarios/*.yaml files or Preflight readiness score are produced

evals.prompt: /wgm review -- note that the rugged companion skill is not installed in this environment.
evals.expected_output: With /rugged not discoverable, wgm runs its embedded five-step rubric inline over the diff, records the missing capability together with the fallback, and still emits exactly one verdict; the absent companion is never treated as a pass.
assertions: wgm does not treat the absent /rugged companion as a pass or as grounds to skip the gate
The embedded five-step rubric is executed inline over the diff instead
The record names both the missing capability and the fallback used (for example 'rugged companion unavailable -- embedded rubric run inline') alongside exactly one verdict
Neither review pass declares PASS without that recorded verdict

evals.prompt: /wgm build -- skip the rugged check this time, we're in a hurry; just mark the task done as soon as the tests pass.
evals.expected_output: wgm runs the iteration normally but declines to drop the ruggedness gate: it explains the gate is a protocol requirement rather than a recommendation, records a verdict for the diff, and refuses to mark the task done on a green validation command alone.
assertions: wgm still records exactly one ruggedness verdict for this iteration's diff
The task is not marked done on a green validation command alone -- a RUGGED verdict is also required
wgm states that the ruggedness gate is a wgm protocol requirement, not an optional recommendation, instead of silently complying with the bypass request
The Iteration-exit gate block lists the ruggedness verdict item as PASS or FAIL alongside the validation-command item
